preserveSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Brooklyn Ochoa. Social worker. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Boot stone, Grandfather's Rope, Beat-up Paperback, Trail compass, Dispatcher's headset. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
A cold snap. Breath smokes. The woods go quiet.
You eat Dried meat and Trail mix (1400 kcal).
👂 Overheard — A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair: "Good. I'll take the first rotation. Somebody has to."
You give A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair 3 portions of Dried beans, with the village watching. They look at you differently now.
🍽️ Zoltan eyes the groaning pantry shelves and packs light today. "No point hauling what'll rot. Mending the nets instead."
👂 Overheard — Brayden: "If we rotate the watch, nobody pulls two nights running. Fair's fair."
You see smoke on the horizon. Emberhold — 11 people, 3 days in. foragers, by the look of it. They know 2 plants — 2 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
